judgment.notes: Defines every Euclidean ambient space, the singleton R^0, Borel structure, and coordinate-adjoining identification with the Euclidean square-sum distance. This preserves the prescribed metric and introduces no product-norm equivalence assumption or target conclusion.

Extended diameter, empty-set value, and identification of finite values with nonnegative reals are unambiguous. The stated zero-diameter singleton fact follows directly: every pair has distance ≤0, hence consists of equal points. No boundedness is assumed for arbitrary sets.

Specifies arbitrary countable covers, positive real exponent and finite positive real scale, diameter constraint, zero empty-member cost, and extended nonnegative infimum/sum/supremum. This is exactly the supplied unnormalized content and limiting measure. Infimum is defined even without a selected minimizing cover; existence of useful covers is not granted by the definition.

Names the pinned native Hausdorff measure, with the diameter-power gauge, scale construction, Borel realization, and outer-measure interpretation on arbitrary sets. Readback of Hausdorff.lean:412-434,464-469,535-552 confirms the construction and zero empty-member cost. At exponent zero the nonempty singleton gauge is 1. Generic use carries the canonical Borel structure; M002–M004 explicitly retain its measurable/Borel hypotheses. Equality with D003 is reserved for N001.

The supremum over finite nonnegative exponents with infinite Hausdorff measure agrees with native dimH (readback HausdorffDimension.lean:94-112); its codomain and supremum-empty value are explicit. Critical-exponent and D003-agreement claims are expressly proof obligations, exported by N001, not hidden axioms.
The closed unit interval is explicitly a subset of R with both endpoints. This matches the target and has no construction guard.

F is exactly E×I transported by D001 to Eucl(n+1). Its dependencies give the required ambient space and metric; existence is set formation, with no assumption of nonemptiness, compactness, or dimension built into the name.

D abbreviates dimH(E) as an extended nonnegative real, so its definition does not assume finiteness or D≤n. N002 exports those assertions; the upper-bound, positive-D lower-bound, and final-assembly edges directly include N002. The zero-D branch has the explicit antecedent D=0, which itself ensures finiteness. There is no undefined choice of a finite representative at definition time.

Specifies the usual existing Lebesgue measure, its interval-length normalization, Borel indicators, extended nonnegative integrals, and restriction to I. The listed interval values are the standard normalization of this measure, not additional conditions on E or a substitute for Tonelli. No measurability of arbitrary covering sets or projections is assumed; the supplied route introduces open interval enlargements. Further integral manipulations remain local mathematical obligations.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
